A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
Reset needs a defined idle level. Many parts have an internal pull-up, which is why this is a warning rather than an error.
VDDA feeds the ADC and the internal reference. It gets its own local capacitor, not a share of the digital rail's.
The analogue rail wants a bulk capacitor of its own alongside the 100nF.
BOOT0 selects whether the part runs user flash or the bootloader. Left floating the board boots into the bootloader some of the time.
When no backup cell is fitted VBAT is tied to VDD and still wants its own local capacitor.

rules.why: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
Strapping pins are sampled once at reset. Floating, they decide the boot mode at random and the part comes up differently between boards.

Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
Strapping pins are sampled once at reset. Floating, they decide the boot mode at random and the part comes up differently between boards.

companions.why: Each supply pin needs a local ceramic to supply the switching current the rail cannot deliver fast enough; without it the die sees its own supply collapse on every edge.
One bulk capacitor per device holds the rail up through load steps the decoupling caps are too small for.
A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
Reset needs a defined idle level. Many parts have an internal pull-up, which is why this is a warning rather than an error.
VDDA feeds the ADC and the internal reference. It gets its own local capacitor, not a share of the digital rail's.
The analogue rail wants a bulk capacitor of its own alongside the 100nF.
BOOT0 selects whether the part runs user flash or the bootloader. Left floating the board boots into the bootloader some of the time.
When no backup cell is fitted VBAT is tied to VDD and still wants its own local capacitor.

A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
Reset needs a defined idle level. Many parts have an internal pull-up, which is why this is a warning rather than an error.
VDDA feeds the ADC and the internal reference. It gets its own local capacitor, not a share of the digital rail's.
The analogue rail wants a bulk capacitor of its own alongside the 100nF.
VCAP is the internal core regulator's output brought out only so this capacitor can stabilise it. Without it the core regulator does not start.
BOOT0 selects whether the part runs user flash or the bootloader. Left floating the board boots into the bootloader some of the time.
When no backup cell is fitted VBAT is tied to VDD and still wants its own local capacitor.

rules.why: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
Strapping pins are sampled once at reset. Floating, they decide the boot mode at random and the part comes up differently between boards.

A capacitor on reset stretches the release past the supply's rise and keeps noise off the pin.
Reset needs a defined idle level. Many parts have an internal pull-up, which is why this is a warning rather than an error.
VDDA feeds the ADC and the internal reference. It gets its own local capacitor, not a share of the digital rail's.
The analogue rail wants a bulk capacitor of its own alongside the 100nF.
BOOT0 selects whether the part runs user flash or the bootloader. Left floating the board boots into the bootloader some of the time.
When no backup cell is fitted VBAT is tied to VDD and still wants its own local capacitor.

rules.why: A supply or return pin that reaches no net means the part is unpowered.
A floating input sits at an undefined level and picks up whatever is nearby.
Pins the symbol groups into one domain landing on different nets is usually a wiring slip, occasionally deliberate.
Strapping pins are sampled once at reset. Floating, they decide the boot mode at random and the part comes up differently between boards.
